common: Bush rose SEE YOU® in Rosé
visual: Compact bushy Persica-hybrid rose with dark green foliage and masses of fragrant, semi-double soft pink flowers, each with a striking dark reddish-pink eye and bright yellow stamens.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during prolonged dry periods; established plants are comparatively drought tolerant for a garden rose.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained neutral to alkaline soil.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging and planting directly into soil recently occupied by another rose unless the soil is renewed.
prune: Prune in early spring, removing dead, weak or crossing growth and reducing strong stems to maintain a compact bush. Deadhead to encourage repeat flowering.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems can scratch skin; wear gloves when pruning.
resilience: Exceptionally winter hardy and bred from drought-adapted Persica genetics; vigorous repeat flowering and useful for pollinators.
uses: Bush rose, patio container, sunny border, pollinator garden, low informal planting and cut flowers.
uncertain: Kordes describes higher susceptibility to black spot than some UK launch material, which broadly promotes the cultivar as disease-resistant; pestRisk has therefore been kept moderate rather than unusually low.

visual: Low spreading ground-cover rose with glossy healthy green foliage and large sprays of vivid pink semi-double flowers produced repeatedly through summer and autumn.
water: Water regularly while establishing; established plants tolerate short dry spells but flower best with reliable moisture.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged ground. Renew soil if planting where roses have recently grown to reduce rose replant problems.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring by removing damaged growth and shortening or shearing stems to control spread. Deadheading is optional.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems can scratch skin; wear gloves when handling.
cvs: Flower Carpet Pink / Pink Flower Carpet / Noatraum
resilience: Vigorous, exceptionally disease-resistant for a rose and tolerant of exposed positions once established.
uses: Ground cover, banks and slopes, mass planting, low hedging, borders and large containers.
uncertain: RHS uses Pink Flower Carpet and Flower Carpet Pink as trade synonyms associated with cultivar 'Noatraum'.

visual: Small compact patio rose with glossy mid-green foliage and clusters of neat, lightly scented pure-white flowers produced repeatedly from summer into autumn.
water: Keep evenly moist during active growth, particularly in containers, but allow excess water to drain freely.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Container plants dry rapidly in summer but should never remain waterlogged. Avoid planting directly into an old rose planting hole without renewing soil.
prune: Prune lightly in late winter or early spring, removing weak or damaged growth and shortening remaining stems. Deadhead regularly.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Cold hardy but, like other miniature and patio roses, requires consistent watering and feeding when confined to containers.
uses: Patio pot, balcony, courtyard, front of border, small garden and seasonal flowering display.
uncertain: RHS currently lists the cultivar-name status of 'White Patio' as unresolved, but the plant itself has a defined RHS profile.

visual: Compact floribunda with glossy green foliage and generous clusters of small semi-double bright scarlet-red flowers with conspicuous golden-yellow stamens and a light fragrance.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during prolonged dry spells, directing water towards the soil rather than repeatedly wetting foliage.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging and planting directly into soil recently occupied by another rose without first renewing the soil.
prune: Prune in early spring, removing weak, dead or crossing stems and shortening healthy shoots to around 25–30 cm where appropriate. Deadhead spent clusters.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems can scratch skin; gloves are recommended.
resilience: Compact, vigorous and noted for very good foliage health and disease resistance.
uses: Gift rose, patio container, front of border, mass planting, pollinator planting and small gardens.
uncertain: RHS associates Grandpa's Rose with the trade name Canzonetta and cultivar 'Noa84497D'.
The RHS cultivar page currently contains limited cultivation detail; the H6-level cold tolerance is supported by European cultivation information reporting frost tolerance to roughly −23°C.

visual: Compact floribunda with bushy green foliage and abundant clusters of lightly fragrant red double flowers with a paler centre and distinctive silvery reverse to the petals.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during dry weather; avoid repeatedly wetting flowers and foliage late in the day.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging and rose-replant soil without renewal or substantial improvement.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring, removing dead and weak stems and cutting healthy growth back to maintain a compact floribunda shape. Deadhead regularly.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems can scratch skin; wear gloves when pruning.
resilience: Hardy, free-flowering and reported to have good disease resistance.
uses: Gift rose, border, bedding, patio container, cut flowers and small gardens.
uncertain: There are other roses sold internationally under the name 'My Mum'; the UK red-and-silver floribunda on current garden-centre labels is Rosa 'Webmorrow'.

visual: Classic upright hybrid tea rose with dark reddish-green foliage and large, beautifully formed deep coral-red flowers renowned for their exceptionally intense fragrance.
water: Water deeply during dry weather, especially while establishing and during bud development.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged soil and very exposed sites. Renew soil when replacing an old rose to reduce replant disease.
prune: Prune firmly in late winter or early spring, removing weak and damaged stems and reducing vigorous healthy shoots. Deadhead repeat blooms through the season.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems can scratch skin; wear gloves when handling.
resilience: Cold hardy and vigorous but requires normal monitoring for black spot, mildew, rust and common rose pests.
uses: Fragrance garden, cut flowers, mixed border, rose bed and large patio container.

visual: Bushy English shrub rose bearing exceptionally full pale pink flowers with warm apricot-yellow centres, fading towards cream and carrying a strong tea and old-rose fragrance.
water: Water deeply during prolonged dry periods and regularly through the first growing season.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging. When replacing an established rose, renew the planting soil to reduce rose replant disease.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring to retain a balanced open shrub, removing dead or weak stems and shortening healthy growth. Deadhead during flowering.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin; gloves are recommended.
resilience: Strong, healthy upright growth and good UK hardiness; as with other roses, monitor for aphids and fungal diseases.
uses: Shrub border, rose hedge, fragrance garden, patio container, cottage garden and cut flowers.

visual: Rounded English shrub rose with glossy dark green foliage and large cupped rich-yellow flowers that soften towards creamy yellow with age, carrying a powerful fruity fragrance with lemon notes.
water: Water deeply during dry periods and regularly while establishing, particularly when container grown.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid stagnant wet soil. If planting where another rose previously grew, replace or substantially renew the surrounding soil.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring to retain a rounded open framework, removing damaged or weak stems and shortening healthy shoots. Deadhead for repeat flowering.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin; gloves are recommended.
resilience: Cold hardy and repeat flowering with vigorous, rounded shrub growth; normal rose pest and fungal monitoring is advisable.
uses: Fragrance garden, shrub border, cottage garden, cut flowers, rose bed and large containers.

visual: Small elegant upright Japanese maple with exceptionally long, narrow strap-like lobes, emerging and remaining rich wine-red before turning brilliant scarlet-red in autumn.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing and during dry summer periods; container plants require particularly consistent watering.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or mildly alkaline.
soilWarning: Protect from hot drying winds, severe exposure and prolonged drought, which can scorch the finely divided foliage. Avoid waterlogging.
prune: Requires little pruning. Remove dead, damaged or badly placed branches while dormant and avoid heavy pruning during active sap flow.
resilience: Very cold hardy but the delicate narrow foliage is vulnerable to wind scorch, drought and late frost damage.
uses: Japanese garden, courtyard, specimen tree, sheltered border, bonsai-style planting and large container.

visual: Compact bushy floribunda with glossy mid-green foliage and lightly scented double flowers opening in rich apricot and orange shades before gradually maturing through softer pink tones.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during prolonged dry weather, watering deeply at soil level.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid persistent waterlogging and replace or substantially improve soil where another rose has recently grown.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring, removing weak, damaged or crossing stems and shortening healthy growth. Deadhead regularly to encourage repeat flowering.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin; wear gloves when handling.
resilience: Robust and repeat flowering; may still be affected by common rose pests and fungal diseases including black spot and powdery mildew.
uses: Patio container, front or middle of border, rose bed, cut flowers and cottage garden.

visual: Compact patio rose with glossy dark green foliage and clusters of small cupped double flowers in delicate light shell-pink, accompanied by a gentle fragrance.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing and during dry periods, particularly when grown in containers.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging. Container plants need reliable summer watering without sitting permanently wet.
prune: Lightly prune in late winter or early spring to maintain a compact framework and remove weak or damaged growth. Deadhead throughout flowering.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Compact, robust and exceptionally long flowering, though normal rose pest and fungal monitoring is still advisable.
uses: Patio pot, wedding or gift rose, edging, front of border, low hedge and cut flowers.
uncertain: Lovely Bride is also sold under the trade names Lovely Meilland and Lovely Meidiland; 'Meiratcan' is the cultivar name.

visual: Low spreading rose with rich dark green foliage and abundant clusters of lightly fragrant semi-double flowers in glowing orange-red and warm sunset tones from summer well into autumn.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate short dry spells but flower best with reliable moisture.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging. Renew soil when replacing an established rose to reduce rose replant problems.
prune: Trim in late winter or early spring to control spread and remove dead or damaged growth. Deadheading is optional but can keep plants tidy.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Repeat flowering and specifically noted for strong disease resistance; suitable for relatively low-maintenance ground-cover planting.
uses: Ground cover, banks, slopes, mass planting, borders, low landscaping and containers.
uncertain: Some nursery material spells the cultivar code 'Deseoo', but RHS records Flower Carpet Sunset as Rosa 'Deseo'.

visual: Low bushy ground-cover rose with glossy dark green foliage and large clusters of lightly scented semi-double ruby-red to bright pink-red flowers with prominent golden stamens.
water: Water regularly until established and during prolonged dry periods; mature plants tolerate moderate drying between waterings.
soil: Moderately fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and renew soil where roses have recently been grown.
prune: Trim in late winter or early spring to control shape and remove damaged stems. Ground-cover plants can tolerate straightforward shearing when necessary.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Vigorous repeat-flowering ground-cover rose with strong garden performance and good disease resistance.
uses: Ground cover, banks and slopes, mass planting, front of borders, wildlife planting and containers.
uncertain: Flower Carpet Ruby is also sold as Heidefeuer; RHS associates both names with cultivar 'Noafeuer'.

visual: Compact arching ground-cover rose with glossy green foliage and prolific clusters of single coral-pink flowers with paler centres, repeating from late spring through autumn.
water: Water regularly while establishing, then during prolonged dry periods; avoid leaving the roots permanently saturated.
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained clay, loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged soil and renew soil where another rose has recently grown.
prune: Lightly trim in late winter or early spring to maintain a dense spreading habit and remove dead or damaged growth.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Hardy, long flowering and well suited to low-maintenance ground-cover use, with the Flower Carpet range selected for strong garden disease resistance.
uses: Ground cover, banks and slopes, borders, wildlife gardens, mass planting and patio containers.
uncertain: RHS lists 'Noala' and 'Alfabia' as synonyms associated with Flower Carpet Coral.

visual: Vigorous repeat-flowering rambler with flexible arching stems, dark green foliage and large clusters of small fully double pale pink flowers produced repeatedly from summer into autumn.
water: Water deeply while establishing and during prolonged dry spells, especially when growing against a wall where soil may remain comparatively dry.
soil: Moderately fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid persistent waterlogging. Roses planted beside walls may need extra watering because foundations create a rain shadow.
prune: After establishment, remove one or two older stems periodically and shorten flowered side shoots. Tie flexible new shoots horizontally where possible to encourage additional flowering shoots.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Prickly stems may scratch skin; wear gloves when pruning or training.
resilience: Cold hardy, vigorous and repeat flowering; may still be affected by common rose pests and fungal diseases.
uses: Wall, fence, pergola, arch, pillar, large container and weeping standard.
uncertain: Despite its delicate name, Super Fairy is a repeat-flowering rambler/climber rather than a small patio or ground-cover rose.

visual: Bushy floribunda with mahogany-tinted dark green foliage and spectacular fully double yellow flowers irregularly striped, streaked and splashed with bright orange, giving every bloom a slightly different pattern.
water: Water deeply during prolonged dry weather and regularly through the first growing season.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and renew soil if replacing an established rose to reduce replant disease.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring as a floribunda, removing weak or damaged stems and shortening healthy shoots. Deadhead regularly for repeat flowering.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin; wear gloves when pruning.
resilience: Hardy and vigorous, though susceptible to the usual rose pests and diseases including aphids, black spot, rust and powdery mildew.
uses: Mixed border, rose bed, cottage garden, specimen shrub and cut flowers.

visual: Compact upright English shrub rose with pink-tinged buds opening into large clusters of soft pale-yellow cupped flowers, paling almost white at the petal edges around a richer yellow centre.
water: Water deeply while establishing and during prolonged dry weather, keeping the root zone evenly moist without waterlogging.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging and renew soil where roses have recently been grown to reduce rose replant problems.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring as a shrub rose, removing weak or damaged stems and shortening healthy growth to maintain a balanced open framework. Deadhead for repeat flowering.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin; wear gloves when handling.
resilience: Cold hardy and free flowering; normal monitoring for aphids, black spot, rust and powdery mildew is advisable.
uses: Shrub border, fragrance garden, cut flowers, cottage garden, rose hedge and large containers.

visual: Rounded vigorous English shrub rose with dark green foliage, mulberry-purple young stems and large many-petalled rosette flowers in rich deep pink, accompanied by a powerful fruity fragrance.
water: Water deeply during establishment and prolonged dry spells, particularly during flowering.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid persistent waterlogging and refresh soil when replacing an old rose.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring to maintain a rounded open shrub, removing weak, dead or crossing stems and shortening healthy shoots.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems can scratch skin.
resilience: Vigorous and cold hardy with strong repeat flowering; may still encounter common rose pests and fungal diseases.
uses: Shrub border, fragrance garden, cut flowers, cottage garden and informal hedge.

common: English rose Princess Alexandra of Kent
visual: Rounded English shrub rose producing exceptionally large, fully petalled rich bright-pink flowers, deeper towards the centre, with a powerful fresh tea fragrance developing lemon and blackcurrant notes.
water: Water thoroughly during dry weather and regularly during the first growing season.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and replace exhausted soil where another rose has recently grown.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring as a shrub rose, removing dead or weak growth and reducing healthy shoots to retain a balanced rounded framework.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Hardy, robust and repeat flowering; common rose pests and fungal diseases remain possible.
uses: Shrub border, fragrance garden, cut flowers, low hedge and large containers.

visual: Compact dense Japanese maple with clusters of bright red spring foliage that deepens to dark red through summer before glowing brilliant crimson again in autumn.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing and water during prolonged summer dryness, particularly in containers.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained acidic to neutral soil.
soilWarning: Protect from drying winds and severe exposure. Lack of soil moisture or intense exposed sun can scorch the foliage.
prune: Requires little pruning; remove dead, damaged or poorly placed branches while dormant and avoid unnecessary heavy pruning.
resilience: Very cold hardy, but foliage may scorch in exposed hot or dry conditions; possible problems include aphids, acer gall mite, Verticillium wilt and honey fungus.
uses: Specimen shrub, Japanese garden, courtyard, patio container, rock garden and architectural planting.

visual: Tall airy English shrub rose carrying generous heads of fragrant semi-double cupped flowers that open rich apricot and soften through peach and lighter apricot tones.
water: Water deeply while establishing and during prolonged periods of hot dry weather.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid persistent waterlogging and renew soil when planting into a former rose position.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring, maintaining its naturally tall open framework while removing weak, damaged or congested growth.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems can scratch skin.
resilience: Hardy and notably tolerant of heat and relatively dry conditions once established, with reliable repeat flowering.
uses: Back or middle of border, informal hedge, cottage garden, wildlife garden and cut flowers.

visual: Compact upright English shrub rose with abundant fully double soft-apricot cupped flowers and a distinctive fruity fragrance with notes of lemon, lychee and fresh apricot.
water: Water deeply while establishing and during prolonged dry conditions; container plants require more regular watering.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and renew soil when planting where roses previously grew.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring to retain a compact upright shape, removing weak and damaged stems and shortening healthy shoots.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Healthy compact rose that performs in partial shade and containers as well as borders.
uses: City garden, patio container, border, rose hedge, wall-side planting and fragrance garden.

visual: Compact patio rose with glossy dark green foliage and abundant clusters of lightly scented, frilled double mid-pink flowers produced repeatedly through summer.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing and when container grown; water more deeply during prolonged hot weather.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging and do not allow small containers to dry completely during summer.
prune: Prune lightly in late winter or early spring as a patio rose, removing weak or damaged shoots and shortening healthy stems.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Fairly disease resistant, tolerant of poorer soils and particularly well suited to containers and small gardens.
uses: Patio container, front of border, low hedge, courtyard, gift rose and cut flowers.

visual: Compact upright floribunda with glossy dark green foliage and lightly scented double flowers in vibrant brassy yellow strongly flushed and edged coppery orange-red, with the red tones intensifying in bright sun.
water: Water deeply during establishment and prolonged dry periods, particularly when grown in containers.
soil: Moderately fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and renew soil where roses have previously grown.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring as a floribunda, reducing healthy stems by roughly one-third to one-half and removing congested, crossing or damaged growth.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Compact repeat-flowering rose selected for excellent disease resistance and healthy glossy foliage.
uses: Rose bed, mixed border, patio container, mass planting and cut flowers.
uncertain: An older unrelated rose has also been registered under the name 'Meteor'; this card uses the current Kordes floribunda 'Korzeigar', marketed as Meteor and Rose of the Year 2024.

visual: Bushy evergreen shrub with dark green oval leaves broadly edged creamy white, often developing attractive pink flushing during colder weather.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate moderate dry periods but perform best with consistent moisture.
soil: Moist but well-drained or well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging. Reverted shoots with plain green foliage should be removed promptly.
prune: Requires little pruning; trim to shape during spring or summer and remove reverted green shoots completely at their origin.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten. Wear gloves when handling, particularly if skin is sensitive.
resilience: Hardy, adaptable and tolerant of exposed conditions; possible problems include vine weevil, caterpillars, scale insects and powdery mildew.
uses: Evergreen structure, hedge, ground cover, banks, borders, wall-side planting and containers.
uncertain: Euonymus fortunei f. radicans 'Silver Queen' and Euonymus japonicus 'Silver Queen' are older synonyms used for this plant.

visual: Broad bushy repeat-flowering rose with glossy dark green foliage and prolific clusters of semi-double vivid deep-pink flowers with paler centres and exposed golden-yellow stamens.
water: Water deeply while establishing and during prolonged dry weather, allowing the upper soil to begin drying between waterings.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid persistent waterlogging and renew planting soil where roses have recently been grown.
prune: Prune in late winter or early spring, removing damaged, weak or congested stems and shortening healthy growth to maintain a dense bushy framework.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin.
resilience: Strong repeat flowering, glossy foliage and very good disease resistance, with a vigorous broadly bushy habit.
uses: Flower border, low shrub planting, mass planting, wildlife garden and large containers.
uncertain: Several unrelated roses have historically been sold as 'Rosy Cheeks'. This card uses the current UK nursery plant Rosa 'Noa200051', which matches the surrounding cultivars in this batch.
'Noa200051' is also marketed in continental Europe as Residenz.

visual: Dwarf hardy cyclamen with rounded silver-patterned foliage and numerous small rose-pink flowers with swept-back petals, providing vivid colour through the depths of winter.
water: Keep moderately moist during active autumn and winter growth, then allow conditions to become somewhat drier as the foliage dies back.
soil: Humus-rich, fertile, sharply well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid excessive summer moisture and stagnant winter wet around the tuber. Best in partial shade beneath deciduous trees or shrubs.
prune: No pruning required; remove spent foliage only once it has naturally died back.
toxicity: Tubers are harmful if eaten. Wear gloves when handling if sensitive.
resilience: Very winter hardy in suitable free-draining soil; possible problems include mice, squirrels, vine weevil and cyclamen grey mould.
uses: Woodland garden, winter container, underplanting shrubs, shady border, rock garden and naturalising.
uncertain: The supplied label 'Rose Silver Leaf' resolves most closely to Cyclamen coum Cyberia Rose Silver.
RHS currently lists the cultivar-name status as unresolved; Syngenta and the Cyclamen Society both recognise Cyberia Rose Silver within the Cyberia Series.
H5 follows RHS hardiness for Cyclamen coum because RHS does not publish a cultivar-specific hardiness rating.

visual: Suckering deciduous shrub grown primarily for brilliant crimson-red young stems in winter, with green summer foliage turning plum-red in autumn, cream flower clusters and bluish-white berries.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants perform best with reliable moisture but tolerate ordinary garden conditions.
soil: Moist but well-drained or well-drained clay, loam or sandy soil; acid to neutral.
soilWarning: Best winter stem colour is produced by strong young growth. Avoid extremely dry soil if vigorous replacement shoots are wanted.
prune: For the brightest winter stems, cut established plants hard in early spring, removing old stems close to the base to encourage vigorous new red shoots.
resilience: Exceptionally cold hardy and adaptable; generally pest-free although horse chestnut scale, cornus anthracnose and honey fungus can occasionally occur.
uses: Winter stem display, wildlife garden, informal hedge, mass planting, coastal garden and cut stems.
uncertain: Baton Rouge is the trade designation; 'Minbat' is the cultivar name.

visual: Compact evergreen hellebore with leathery dark green foliage and distinctive pink flowers intricately patterned with fine burgundy-red speckles and lines radiating from the centre.
water: Keep moderately and consistently moist while establishing, particularly during active growth and flowering.
soil: Rich, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; neutral to alkaline preferred.
soilWarning: Avoid stagnant winter wet and very dry exposed positions. Performs especially well in partial shade beneath deciduous trees and shrubs.
prune: Remove old or damaged foliage before or as flowers emerge to display blooms clearly and reduce disease carry-over; remove spent flower stems if seed is not wanted.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten and sap may irritate skin; wear gloves when handling.
resilience: Long-lived and very cold hardy once established; generally robust in moisture-retentive but freely draining soil.
uses: Winter border, woodland garden, underplanting deciduous shrubs, patio container and cut flowers.
uncertain: ViV identifies Celestina as a named selection but an independent registered cultivar epithet was not located.
Published exact-plant hardiness information ranges from approximately −18°C to an H7 nursery rating; H6 is used conservatively.

visual: Upright clump-forming perennial producing large fragrant panicles of pale shell-pink flowers, each dramatically marked with a deep pink to crimson central eye.
water: Keep consistently moist during active growth and flowering, watering at soil level during prolonged dry periods.
soil: Fertile, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid severe summer drought and overcrowding. Good airflow and watering at the base help reduce mildew problems.
prune: Deadhead to prolong flowering, then cut stems back to ground level in autumn.
resilience: Extremely cold hardy and generally pest-free; may occasionally suffer downy mildew or leaf spot.
uses: Cottage garden, perennial border, prairie planting, pollinator garden and cut flowers.

visual: Vigorous low evergreen heath forming a dense mat of dark bronze-green needle-like foliage covered with deep magenta flowers from winter into spring.
water: Water regularly until established; mature plants need only moderate watering except during prolonged drought.
soil: Moist but well-drained to well-drained acidic or neutral soil.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and strongly alkaline conditions.
prune: Lightly trim immediately after flowering, cutting only into leafy growth and avoiding old bare wood.
resilience: Generally pest-free and very dependable in winter; wet conditions can encourage Phytophthora root rot and other fungal diseases.
uses: Winter colour, ground cover, banks, slopes, rock garden and containers.

visual: Low spreading evergreen heath with foliage emerging pale green before turning luminous golden yellow, complemented by masses of magenta-pink flowers from winter into spring.
water: Water regularly until established, then moderately during extended dry periods.
soil: Well-drained or moist but well-drained acidic to neutral soil.
soilWarning: Avoid strongly alkaline soil and persistent winter waterlogging.
prune: Lightly trim after flowering to maintain a compact dense habit, avoiding cuts into old leafless wood.
resilience: Generally pest-free and tolerant of exposed conditions; excessive wet can cause root-rotting fungal diseases.
uses: Winter garden, ground cover, edging, rock garden, coastal planting and containers.

visual: Aromatic evergreen dwarf shrub with soft grey-green leaves dramatically splashed and edged yellow to golden cream, plus pale purplish-blue flowers in summer.
water: Water while establishing, then sparingly; established plants are drought tolerant.
soil: Moderately fertile, well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Protect from excessive winter wet. Heavy waterlogged soil can cause root and foot rots.
prune: Trim lightly in spring to maintain compact growth and remove flower spikes after flowering; avoid cutting deeply into old bare wood.
resilience: Drought tolerant once established; possible pests include rosemary beetle, sage leafhopper and capsid bug.
uses: Culinary herb garden, Mediterranean planting, gravel garden, wildlife garden, edging and containers.
uncertain: The supplied OCR 'Icteniwa sage' resolves confidently to Salvia officinalis 'Icterina'.

visual: Aromatic semi-evergreen culinary sage with rich purple young leaves and stems that mature through grey-purple to grey-green, accompanied by purple-blue flowers in summer.
water: Water while establishing, then only during extended dry weather; mature plants are drought tolerant.
soil: Moderately fertile, well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Protect from excessive winter wet and avoid heavy waterlogged ground.
prune: Trim lightly in spring and remove spent flower stems after flowering to maintain compact bushy growth.
resilience: Drought tolerant once established; possible problems include rosemary beetle, leafhopper, powdery mildew and root rots in wet soil.
uses: Culinary herb garden, Mediterranean planting, gravel garden, pollinator garden and containers.
uncertain: The supplied label 'Purple Sage' is interpreted as the standard culinary purple sage Salvia officinalis 'Purpurascens'.

visual: Upright aromatic culinary perennial with slender glossy green leaves carrying the characteristic sweet anise-like flavour of true French tarragon and inconspicuous pale yellow summer flowerheads.
water: Water moderately while establishing and during sustained dry periods, allowing soil to drain freely between waterings.
soil: Light, well-drained loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Struggles in heavy poorly drained ground, especially during winter. A warm sheltered position improves reliability.
prune: Cut old stems back to the lowest fresh shoots in mid to late spring and harvest growing tips regularly during the season.
resilience: Generally pest-free but dislikes prolonged winter wet; may occasionally be affected by honey fungus.
uses: Culinary herb garden, raised bed, sunny border, gravel garden and containers.
uncertain: The supplied OCR 'Frevch rarrac' is interpreted as French tarragon.
RHS lists Artemisia dracunculus 'Sativa' and var. sativa as synonyms for French tarragon.

visual: Compact aromatic oregano with small green leaves broadly edged creamy white, creating a bright variegated mound topped by loose sprays of tiny pink flowers in summer.
water: Water moderately while establishing; mature plants prefer relatively dry conditions and tolerate short droughts.
soil: Sharply well-drained chalk or loam; acid, neutral or alkaline, with alkaline soil preferred.
soilWarning: Avoid heavy wet ground, especially in winter. Variegation is most attractive where plants receive good light.
prune: Cut old flowered stems back in early spring and trim lightly after flowering if required.
resilience: Hardy, drought tolerant once established and generally disease-free; leafhoppers may occasionally occur.
uses: Herb garden, rock garden, gravel garden, edging, coastal garden and containers.

visual: Very compact rounded autumn perennial covered in masses of medium-sized semi-double light pink daisy flowers with contrasting yellow centres.
water: Keep moderately and consistently moist during active growth, particularly in containers.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained garden soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid stagnant water and overcrowding. Good airflow helps reduce fungal disease.
prune: Deadhead if desired and cut old stems down after flowering or once growth dies back.
resilience: Compact first-year-flowering selection bred for a naturally rounded habit without pinching; hardy when established.
uses: Autumn container, edging, front of border, mass planting and pollinator garden.
uncertain: Florensis sells this within the older Aster dumosus Alpha® series; modern botanical taxonomy places Aster dumosus within Symphyotrichum dumosum.
Florensis describes the series simply as hardy without an RHS hardiness number, so H6 is a conservative UK estimate.

visual: Compact sturdy coneflower producing vivid tangerine-orange daisy-like flowers with distinctive lime-green to orange central cones from midsummer into autumn.
water: Water regularly while establishing; once established, water during prolonged drought while allowing the soil to drain freely.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid heavy waterlogged soil, especially over winter. Echinacea resent excessive root disturbance.
prune: Deadhead regularly to encourage further blooms, or leave late seedheads standing for birds before cutting back.
resilience: Hardy, heat tolerant and generally pest- and disease-free once established; strongly attractive to pollinating insects.
uses: Sunny border, prairie planting, wildlife garden, cut flowers and patio containers.
uncertain: SunSeekers Mineola is the trade designation; 'Ifecssmin' is the cultivar code.

visual: Compact black-eyed Susan with large single daisies, their rich mahogany-maroon petals dramatically tipped golden yellow around a dark chocolate-brown central button.
water: Keep moderately and consistently moist during active growth, particularly during hot weather and when container grown.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained clay or loam; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and very poor airflow, which can encourage grey mould.
prune: Deadhead spent flowers regularly to prolong the flowering display.
resilience: Generally pest-free, but not reliably winter hardy across much of the UK and normally treated as an annual or biennial.
uses: Summer border, patio container, cottage garden, wildlife garden and cut flowers.
uncertain: The supplied 'Kissing SmileyZ' resolves exactly to Rudbeckia hirta 'Kissing Smileyz'.
Although botanically a short-lived perennial, RHS recommends growing it as a half-hardy annual in the UK.

visual: Compact upright to spreading shrub with glossy evergreen or semi-evergreen leaves, emerging bronze before becoming green and developing reddish-purple autumn colour, plus fragrant white summer flowers and red berries ripening black.
water: Water regularly while establishing; established plants prefer moderate, consistent moisture.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained or well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Reliable berry production requires cross-pollination with another compatible Viburnum flowering at the same time.
prune: Requires little pruning; remove damaged or misplaced shoots after flowering and lightly shape if necessary.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten.
resilience: Adaptable and hardy; possible problems include aphids, viburnum beetle, Phytophthora, leaf spot and honey fungus.
uses: Evergreen shrub border, specimen, informal hedge, screening and wildlife garden.
uncertain: The heavily corrupted label fragments around 'MARQUIS / VIBURNUM / LEois' resolve confidently to Viburnum 'Le Bois Marquis'.
RHS describes the plant as evergreen or semi-evergreen, so foliage retention may vary with winter severity.

visual: Low spreading deciduous shrub with foliage darkening from green to deep purple as summer develops, creating a dramatic background for contrasting white trumpet-shaped flowers flushed reddish purple at their bases.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during prolonged dry spells.
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained or well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Foliage develops its richest dark colouring in good light, although plants tolerate partial shade.
prune: Prune immediately after flowering by removing damaged growth and cutting some older flowered shoots back to strong younger stems.
resilience: Very cold hardy and easy to grow; possible problems include capsid bugs, scale insects, eelworms and honey fungus.
uses: Low flowering hedge, border, ground cover, patio container, coastal planting and courtyard.
uncertain: Ebony and Ivory is the trade designation; RHS treats 'Velda' as the cultivar name.

visual: Large upright witch hazel with broad green leaves developing yellow, orange and red autumn tones, followed on bare winter branches by unusual slightly fragrant coppery-red ribbon-like flowers.
water: Maintain reliable moisture while establishing and during summer dry periods; mulch to conserve soil moisture.
soil: Humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained acidic to neutral soil.
soilWarning: Shelter from cold drying winds and avoid severe summer drought. Dislikes shallow chalky or strongly alkaline soil.
prune: Little pruning required; remove dead, damaged or crossing stems after flowering and remove any suckers arising from below the graft.
resilience: Generally pest-free and long-lived; may occasionally suffer coral spot, honey fungus, Phytophthora or powdery mildew.
uses: Winter garden, specimen shrub, woodland edge, city garden and large border.

visual: Compact bushy smoke bush with rounded wavy-edged leaves heavily washed deep purple over dark blue-green, turning fiery orange-red in autumn, with occasional airy silvery-grey smoke-like seedheads.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate moderate dry periods once rooted.
soil: Moist but well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging. Strong sunlight generally intensifies the purple foliage colour.
prune: Usually requires little pruning; remove damaged stems as needed. Plants grown primarily for foliage can be cut back hard in early spring to encourage vigorous large-leaved shoots.
resilience: Generally pest-free and tolerant of a broad range of soils; occasional problems include Verticillium wilt, honey fungus and powdery mildew.
uses: Foliage specimen, mixed border, courtyard, large container and autumn-colour planting.
uncertain: Dusky Maiden is the trade designation; 'Londus' is the cultivar name.

visual: Compact clump-forming perennial producing masses of bright lemon-yellow daisy-like flowers with rounded golden-yellow central cones on branching wiry stems from late summer into autumn.
water: Keep consistently moist during the growing season and water thoroughly during summer dry spells.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Does not perform well in prolonged drought. Avoid allowing container plants to dry completely during summer.
prune: Deadhead regularly to extend flowering; cut old growth back after flowering or once stems die down. Divide every two to three years to maintain vigour.
resilience: Extremely cold hardy and compact enough not to require the support often needed by taller heleniums; possible problems include slugs, snails, eelworm and mildew.
uses: Sunny border, prairie planting, pollinator garden, cut flowers and containers.
uncertain: RHS currently lists the cultivar-name status of 'Lemon Sundae' as unresolved, but provides a full cultivar profile.

visual: Compact repeat-flowering patio rose with dark green foliage and clusters of fragrant, fully double flowers in rich golden to deep yellow.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing and throughout flowering, particularly when grown in containers.
soil: Humus-rich, fertile, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid persistent waterlogging and renew soil if replacing another rose in the same position.
prune: Prune lightly in late winter or early spring as a patio rose, removing weak, damaged and congested growth. Deadhead to encourage continued flowering.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Thorny stems may scratch skin; wear gloves when handling.
resilience: Cold hardy and repeat flowering; may encounter common rose pests and diseases including aphids, black spot, rust and powdery mildew.
uses: Patio container, front of border, courtyard, rose bed and gift plant.
uncertain: Flower Power Gold is the trade designation; 'Fryneon' is the cultivar name.
